items.title: Hideo Kojima Reprises Cyberpunk 2077 Character in Edgerunners 2
items.summary: Kojima voices Hideyoshi Oshima in video game & anime
items.content:
(In)famous video game director Hideo Kojima confirmed on Monday that he performed in the new original net anime series Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 . The director said he is reprising his Cyberpunk 2077 character Hideyoshi Oshima, a braindance producer, in a cameo appearance in the new anime. Kojima also posted a handful of photos of his voice recording session: Image via x.com © 2026 CD PROJEKT RED S.A. CD PROJEKT RED, the CD PROJEKT RED logo, Cyberpunk, Cyberpunk 2077 and the Cyberpunk 2077 logo are trademarks and/or registered trademarks of CD PROJEKT RED S.A. in the US and/or other countries. Image via x.com ©小島秀夫

Kojima made a cameo appearance in CD PROJEKT RED 's 2020 cyberpunk video game Cyberpunk 2077 as Hideyoshi Oshima. The video game itself draws inspiration from the Cyberpunk tabletop role-playing game series created by Mike Pondsmith in 1988. The tabletop game has seen several editions, including Cyberpunk 2013 , Cyberpunk 2020 , Cyberpunk V3.0 , and the latest edition Cyberpunk Red .

Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 is the sequel to the first Cyberpunk: Edgerunners anime , which Studio Trigger produced based on CD PROJEKT RED 's Cyberpunk 2077 game. The first series premiered on Netflix in September 2022.

The Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 anime premiered on October 20 on Netflix .

items.title: Report: Activision Is Working on an Open-World Game With a Reactive Environment and “Emergent Gameplay”
items.summary: Activision is reportedly working on an open-world game with a reactive environment and emergent gameplay, based on a recent job listing.
items.content:
When companies are not busy chasing trends like games as a service, they go after big-budget hits. And very few games can match the sales of the GTA and Cyberpunk 2077 series.

GTA 6 is unrivaled, but its open-world style is used in other games too. Cyberpunk 2077 also made its mark, and more and more games are copying it.

Now, Activision has a new open-world project in the works at Elsewhere, a new studio that has brought in veteran developers from prominent studios like CD Projekt Red and Naughty Dog. The game is built around emergent gameplay, and it looks set to take on the biggest names in the genre.

The Elsewhere project is taking shape, and it is certainly ambitious. In fact, the studio urgently needs staff, as a recent job posting confirms. The posting asks for an Associate Animation Director, who will have two main jobs: creating interactions in a dynamic world and defining emergent gameplay. It never names GTA or Cyberpunk, but the kind of game it describes puts Elsewhere in the same space.

The job description reads, “You’ll help us by guiding the development of scalable animation systems that support emergent gameplay, contextual behaviors, and dynamic world interactions.”

In case you don’t know, emergent gameplay is when a game’s systems, like its AI, physics, and world rules, work together in ways the developers never scripted. Nobody plans the moment ahead of time. It just happens when the systems run into each other, so every player ends up with their own stories.

GTA 5 is the best-known example. Say you pick a fight with a civilian, who runs off and bumps into a gang member. The gang member pulls a gun and accidentally shoots a nearby cop car. Suddenly the police are in a huge shootout with the gang while you just stand back and watch. No one wrote that scene. The game’s AI systems created it on their own.

With that in mind, these are broad terms, but they give us a good idea of what kind of game Elsewhere is making. It seems to also focus on reactive gameplay, like in titles such as Red Dead Redemption 2.

With this kind of gameplay, a lot could happen. Characters could remember what we did, places could change as we move through them, and some NPCs could even want revenge on us, like in the Nemesis System from Shadow of War.

It is hard not to think of two games that already have these features: Cyberpunk 2077 and GTA 5. GTA 6 is expected to go even bigger, with much more ambition and emergent gameplay.

This does not mean Elsewhere wants to copy these games, or even beat them. It just wants to stand next to them, or at least find its own place in the genre they created.

This is also a change in direction for Activision, which is more used to linear experiences like Call of Duty. To find the company’s last true open-world game, we have to go back to 2012, when it released Prototype 2.

As more information about the project becomes available, we’ll make sure to let you guys know here at MP1st.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Update 2.5 Brings Mods to 6 Platforms [2026]
items.summary: Cyberpunk 2077 Update 2.5 adds cross-platform mod support via mod.io on PC, Mac, PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox, and Nintendo Switch 2. Here is whats confirmed.
items.content:
Cyberpunk 2077 is getting cross-platform mod support in Update 2.5, and for the first time, console players will be able to browse and install player-made mods without ever touching a PC. CD Projekt Red confirmed the feature as part of a broader update tied to the arrival of Edgerunners 2 on Netflix, and the official platform list covers PC, Mac, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch 2 , according to patch notes reported by Nintendo Life .

What’s Actually In Cyberpunk 2077 Update 2.5 How mod.io Powers Cross-Platform Mod Support Which Platforms Get Mod Support First Where Nintendo Switch 2 Fits Into the Rollout The Achievement and Trophy Trade-Off Why CD Projekt Red Is Doing This Now How This Compares to The Witcher 3’s Console Mod Support Console Modding’s Slow Build: Some Historical Context The Bethesda.net Era The Shift to Shared Service Platforms Market Impact: What This Means for CD Projekt Red Competitive Landscape: Who Else Is Building Console Mod Ecosystems What’s Still Unconfirmed About Cyberpunk 2077 Update 2.5 What’s Next: Five Predictions for Cross-Platform Cyberpunk 2077 Modding How to Prepare for Mod Support on Console The Bigger Picture for Console Players Frequently Asked Questions Related Coverage The move puts Cyberpunk 2077 Update 2.5 in rare company. Console mod support has existed in pockets for years, but a built-in, cross-platform browsing system that spans six hardware targets at once, including a Nintendo console, is a different scale of ambition. shattered.io first flagged Update 2.5’s existence when the Edgerunners 2 tie-in was announced, and the mod-support detail is the part that’s generating the most discussion among players this week.

Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google

Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.

At the center of the update is a new in-game menu that lets players browse a curated selection of mods and install them directly, without downloading files externally or touching a file system. That’s the headline change, and it’s the one CD Projekt Red is leaning on hardest in its own messaging. The patch notes describe cross-platform mod support as “a first step into cross-platform modding,” language that signals this is an opening move rather than a finished ecosystem, according to reporting from The Verge .

The week's biggest stories in tech, gaming and security, in one email.

That phrasing matters for how players should read this update. CD Projekt Red isn’t claiming console modding is suddenly as deep as PC modding has been for years through Nexus Mods and other community tools. Instead, Update 2.5 opens a narrower, officially sanctioned channel, one that the studio can moderate, curate, and expand incrementally. The announcement is explicit that more mods are planned to become available over time, which reads as an admission that the day-one catalog is a starting point, not the finished product.

Beyond mod support, Update 2.5 is also the vehicle for content tied to Edgerunners 2, the Netflix anime continuation that shattered.io covered in detail in its earlier report on the Netflix and game update pairing . Bundling a major new feature like mod support with a marketing moment tied to a streaming release is a familiar CD Projekt Red playbook: pair a cultural event with a technical one so each amplifies the other’s reach.

The technical backbone of Cyberpunk 2077’s cross-platform mod support is mod.io, a third-party mod distribution platform that several studios have adopted specifically because it’s built to work within console certification rules. Unlike Steam Workshop or Nexus Mods, which were designed around open PC file systems, mod.io operates as a managed layer: developers can expose a curated, sandboxed subset of community content to console players while keeping the kind of file-system access consoles don’t allow locked down.

That distinction explains why this works differently than PC modding. On PC, Cyberpunk 2077 players have had essentially unrestricted mod access since launch, installing anything from cosmetic tweaks to total gameplay overhauls through community tools. On console, through mod.io, the pool is necessarily smaller and more tightly reviewed, because every mod has to pass through a layer that platform holders like Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo are comfortable certifying.

Reporting from PC Guide notes that CD Projekt Red has described the system as working similarly to the console mod support already shipped for The Witcher 3’s remaster. That’s a useful reference point for players who’ve already used Witcher 3’s mod browser on console: the user experience Cyberpunk 2077 ships with in Update 2.5 should feel familiar rather than experimental, because it’s built on groundwork the studio already tested.

Here’s where the Cyberpunk 2077 Update 2.5 rollout gets more nuanced than a single simultaneous launch. The officially listed platforms, PC, Mac, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch 2, all appear in the confirmed feature list. But the available reporting indicates Nintendo Switch 2’s version of the update is not arriving on the same day as the rest. Switch 2 is on the roadmap; it’s just not first in line.

That staggered approach tracks with how CD Projekt Red has handled Switch 2 releases before. The studio has a track record of launching its biggest Cyberpunk 2077 content on PC and the PlayStation and Xbox ecosystems first, then following with the Nintendo version once additional porting and certification work wraps up. shattered.io has tracked that pattern closely around Switch 2 ports generally, including in its breakdown of how Switch 2’s storage requirements shape what kind of content can land on the console and when.

The table above reflects the officially confirmed platform list for Cyberpunk 2077 Update 2.5’s cross-platform mod support as reported by Nintendo Life and corroborated elsewhere. The one open variable is exactly when Switch 2 owners get their turn, and neither CD Projekt Red nor the outlets tracking the story have published a firm date for that yet.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2 lead confirms “half of the quest team” are modders as CDPR strives to continue supporting the next generation of modding
items.summary: CD Projekt Red confirms that the Cyberpunk 2 quest team largely consists of modders as they push to support the next generation of modding.
items.content:
Games Blog About Us Careers Tutorials FAQs All News Features Guides Reviews Fortnite Marvel Rivals Arc Raiders Tutorials FAQs Cyberpunk 2 lead confirms “half of the quest team” are modders as CDPR strives to continue supporting the next generation of modding Published:

CD Projekt Red’s Cyberpunk 2 is years away from release, but fans are still eagerly awaiting the upcoming sequel. As it turns out, a significant number of fans are also actively working on the game with half of the game’s quest team consisting of modders.

Right now, Cyberpunk 2 is still in pre-production with the game’s concepts continually evolving within CDPR’s new Boston studio. While the game appears to be taking the same first-person-only stance as the original , we have no idea what the game’s narrative hook will be.

With that said, Cyberpunk 2 associate game director and former quest design lead on Cyberpunk 2077 confirmed in a recent livestream that much of the new game’s quest team consists of modders from previous CDPR games.

Sasko explained that modding is still “a foot-in-the-door technique, and a gateway into game dev”. While Cyberpunk 2 is moving from RedEngine to Unreal Engine 5 , modders showed how to make content that fits the world and vibe of the RPG franchise, which was invaluable to CDPR’s new studio.

“You can see and you can learn how things are made—how things can be built,” Sasko continued. “We actually hired so many modders [for Cyberpunk 2]. I would say, at this point, half of the quest team is all former modders.”

Sasko explained that these modders aren’t just from Cyberpunk 2077, but prior games as well. “They were are modders before of The Witcher 3, Witcher 2, you know, before we hired them and they’re part of our company, and it’s a wonderful way to actually start your career and really learn and see how to actually built those things.”

For CDPR, this is why modding is so important with the studio hoping to continue supporting modders into the future. If their games support modding and help create new generations of modders, then they’ve in turn created the next generation of CDPR developers as well.

“That’s just another thing that really excited me,” he said. “That we can keep kind of pushing this thing and make it more available for more players.”

The Witcher and Cyberpunk games are not games that require mods to be enjoyed, but modders have created some truly spectacular experiences for both. (I’m proud to announce myself as a strong lover of The Witcher 3 cloaks mods which give Geralt unparalleled pizzaz).

With that said, mods bring additional longevity to pretty much every game that supports modding, and Cyberpunk specifically has hugely benefitted from the work of modders. From new missions to perks and skill tree reworks, it’s understandable why many only play CDPR’s iconic RPG with mods enabled, and hiring those incredible creators is a great step towards creating an unforgettable sequel.

Lewis White is a veteran games journalist with over a decade in the field. Starting with beloved Xbox website ICXM/XboxMAD, Lewis became the Gaming Editor at MSPoweruser before becoming the Editor in Chief of StealthOptional and Gfinityesports. Lewis later jumped to By Gamers For Gamers where he jumped to become EIC of VideoGamer and the host of the New VideoGamer Podcast prior to the website’s acquisition.

Over the years, Lewis has also seen long-form investigative pieces published in outlets such as Eurogamer, PCGamesN, Wireframe, Retro Gamer, Nintendo Life, and EDGE. Now, as the Editor in Chief of FRVR Blog, Lewis strives to bring the same level of quality journalism with interview-led content to the site in both written and audio form with the FRVR Podcast.

With a First Degree BA Hons in Games Journalism and Public Relations, Lewis has been a stable part of the British games press for over a decade, and has frequently displayed his love of Halo, The Elder Scrolls, Fallout, and other games pretty much everywhere he’s worked. And FRVR is no different.

Cyberpunk 2077 has officially teamed up with GUNNAR Optiks for a new collection of gaming eyewear inspired by the futuristic world of Night City. The collection includes the Arasaka , a premium pair of glasses inspired by one of the game's most powerful corporations, alongside designs based on other familiar elements of the franchise. The Arasaka model is priced at $99 , featuring the company's distinctive black-and-red color scheme and officially licensed Cyberpunk 2077 branding.

Each pair also comes with a collection of accessories, including an Arasaka-branded metal case, microfiber pouch and cleaning cloth. The collection also includes glasses based on Dexter DeShawn and Militech. The officially licensed collaboration features GUNNAR’s lens technology designed to reduce digital eye strain while incorporating aesthetics directly inspired by characters and corporations from CD Projekt Red ’s universe.

In response, developers are paying tribute to the legendary RPG studio online, with many calling its games pivotal to their own creative paths.

17-year BioWare veteran and longtime director Michael Gamble shared the studio's news post. "Your support has meant everything to me over the past 17 years at BioWare," he writes.

New Bungie head Josh Deane replied to Gamble's post, saying, "Thank you and to everyone at Bioware who has built worlds that have been such an important part of our lives." In a separate post , Deane adds, "This studio is magical and an existential part of my favorite gaming memories, I refuse to believe this..."

CD Projekt Red veteran Paweł Sasko, a face of the studio to many fans of Cyberpunk 2077 and The Witcher, says "Baldur's Gate 1 and 2 shaped my imagination and the desire to create games. I would have never been here without BioWare igniting the fire in my heart. It inspired me, formed me, enriched my imagination, and for that I will be forever grateful. I will always remember you."

CDPR co-CEO Michał Nowakowski adds , "Bioware has been a massive part of CDPR history. We befriended them when localizing and selling Baldur's Gate games in Poland, Czech, and Slovakia. And later they were [a] great help when lending us their engine for Witcher 1, sharing their wisdom and even giving us a spot at their booth at E3.

Very sad for the people affected, but also sad to see a legendary brand go down. Not a great day in the games industry."

Gamble responded to Nowakowski's post, saying, "Thanks Michal. We've always been fans of you guys. Always will be."

InXile Entertainment head Brian Fargo also commented on the original Baldur's Gate games. "We saw the promise in what they could do," he says of BioWare's days on Shattered Steel, "and they went on to create Baldur's Gate 1 and 2 and become legendary. A sad day indeed. My thoughts are with everyone there today."

Mortal Kombat's Ed Boon is of a similar mind. "Very sorry to hear. They made some amazing games," he says of BioWare's shutdown statement.

Comms director Thomas Puha of Control and Alan Waker studio Remedy sums up the thoughts of many: "RIP BioWare. This was coming but so sad to read. The growing problem for large publishers is that smaller AAA games won’t bring enough money so can’t take the risk on them, but not doing original games? We need those, need new franchises."

items.title: 'Cyberpunk 2077' is getting a huge new co-op mod
items.summary: Cyberpunk 2077 is getting a new co-op mod this week that lets up to eight players team up.
items.content:
By Elijah Gonzalez Published Oct 21, 2026, 12:38 PM EDT Elijah is a freelance news writer at Polygon. He was an associate editor at The A.V. Club and Paste, and has been featured in outlets like Game Informer, Fanbyte, Unwinnable, and more. He loves media in all forms, from fighting games and horror flicks to slow cinema and visual novels. He's from the Greater Boston area. News Up to eight players can sow chaos in NightCoop

Image: CD Projekt Red Add Polygon.com on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover Cyberpunk 2077 Sign in to your Polygon.com account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Night City is having a busy week. Cyberpunk 2077 is getting a major 2.5 update on Oct. 22, coinciding with the recent release of the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 anime. CD Projekt Red just confirmed what’s in 2.5, including new quests, a perk that enables dual wielding, console mod support, and more. However, the game is arguably getting an even bigger update through unofficial channels: Cyberpunk 2077 is receiving multiplayer co-op support via the NightCoop mod.

NightCoop is a fan-made mod that lets up to eight players take on Night City together. A recently released trailer dives into the details, immediately tackling edge cases that almost certainly gave the mod’s programmers a headache. NightCoop will synchronize the world of Cyberpunk 2077 so combat and stealth work seamlessly for all players. This even applies when a partner activates their Sandevistan to slow time, causing others to see them moving with an afterimage like in the anime.

As for choices and dialogue, these are put to a vote, with the majority choice playing out for all players. The trailer culminates in a duo carrying out a heist, with one operating cameras and drones and the other leading a frontal assault. After closed tests, the mod enters open beta on Oct. 23 at 11 a.m. EDT.

According to NightCoop’s website , the mod will also support PvP, which can be toggled by the host. Player-versus-player shootouts will take into account both combatants’ stats and gear, but will even out damage between those of different levels. To set up the mod, players install NightCoop and the library RED4ext . Then the host loads an existing save or creates a new co-op game, and guests join the host’s game as their own V.

CD Projekt Red has long supported fan-modding efforts , taking the unusual step of adding mod support to the console releases of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt and now Cyberpunk 2077 . The game’s RED4ext modding library has a whopping 12.6 million downloads on Nexus Mods, showing just how popular player-made additions have been .

Added Cross-Platform Mod Support, powered by mod.io, a first step into cross-platform modding that allows you to easily browse and install a selection of player-created mods directly from the in-game menu. More mods will become available over time. The feature is available on PC, Mac, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro and Xbox Series X|S.

Upgrading the World

  • Welcome to Paradise! Added a new side quest that takes you on a journey to uncover a mystery and explore Night City on a guided tour narrated by Richard Night. It unlocks after completing The Heist and reaching level 15 Street Cred.

    [/*]

  • Added 12 new Minor Arcana Tarot Cards to discover across Night City. The Tarot menu now has separate sections for Major and Minor Arcana. The new tarot cards are part of a new side quest, an extension of Fool on the Hill, which activates after scanning any of the new cards. Collect them all to get a special reward.

    [/*]

Quality of Life

  • Saves in the “Load Game” menu are now grouped by separate playthroughs.

    [/*]

  • Added item filters to apartment and vehicle stashes.

    [/*]

  • Modded saves in the "Load Game" menu are now marked with a dedicated icon. Please note that achievements and trophies cannot be earned while playing on console from a modded save file.

    [/*]

  • Updated the selection of AMD FSR options. FSR 3 upscaling is no longer included, while FSR 2.1, FSR 4, and FSR 3.1 Frame Generation remain available.

    [/*]

  • Updated the CD PROJEKT RED Account connection, My Rewards and telemetry consent menus.

    [/*]

Technology

  • Added support for DLSS 4.5, including up to 6X Multi Frame Generation or Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, and the 2nd Generation Transformer Model.

    [/*]

  • Added support for glasses-free 3D effects on compatible Samsung Odyssey 3D monitors, along with a Motion Comfort setting that lets you balance 3D depth and viewing comfort.

    [/*]

  • Added support for MetalFX Frame Interpolation on Mac.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle in settings for FSR Anti-Lag 2.

    [/*]

  • Introduced various performance optimizations, including improvements specifically for Ray Tracing.

    [/*]

  • Improved HDR rendering to provide more accurate colors, brightness, and contrast on compatible displays.

    [/*]

Fixes

  • Things Done Changed- Fixed an issue where the Delamain cab could get stuck after crashing into another vehicle, blocking quest progression.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where enabling Film Grain had no effect.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where tagging enemies while scanning could also cause V to crouch or stand up when using certain control schemes.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where controller settings for the Third-Person Camera were missing.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several typos in various languages.

    [/*]

  • Added various other fixes for features and content introduced since Patch 2.1.

    [/*]

items.title: When Is Edgerunners 2 Set? CD Projekt's Cyberpunk Loremaster Confirms
items.summary: CD Projekt Red loremaster Patrick Mills has revealed the exact year Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 takes place, amid speculation from fans about what it means for the ending of Cyberpunk 2077.
items.content:
CD Projekt Red loremaster Patrick Mills has revealed the exact year Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 takes place, amid speculation from fans about what it means for the ending of Cyberpunk 2077.

According to Mills, Season 2 takes place not long after you bite the bullet and finally meet Hanako at Embers in Cyberpunk 2077.

"Ok so the thing is that I am seeing a lot of people assuming S2 takes place before 2077 but it doesn't, it takes place in 2078," Mills confirmed in a post on Bluesky . "Moving things forward, time doesn't stop in Cyberpunk."

Mills previously posted about a misunderstanding he had seen in early reviews of the series, but wanted to wait until it was out before dropping a truth nuke.

In Edgerunners Season 2, powerful corporation Arasaka doesn’t quite have the same pull it did during the events of Cyberpunk 2077 , which is a hint that the anime takes place after the events of the game. There are also some other smaller and bigger details, but like the loremaster, I don’t want to spoil things for you.

Now they know Edgerunners 2 is set just a year after the events of Cyberpunk 2077, fans are trying to work out what it means for the plot of the game . Some believe it suggests certain endings are canon. Or, perhaps it would be better to say, some believe it suggests certain endings are not canon. In truth, Edgerunners 2 doesn't force CD Projekt into making a decision about canon — a bit like Bethesda's position on Fallout canon in the context of the Amazon TV show, which takes place after all the video games.

The world of Cyberpunk is set to expand further, of course, with the in-development Cyberpunk 2 (where and when the game takes place is yet to be announced). There's also a live-action film in the works, although according to CD Projekt, the Cyberpunk 2077 movie won't retrace the game's steps .

Before all that, Cyberpunk 2077 is set for a surprise Edgerunners 2-themed update this week. CD Projekt has confirmed it features cyberware customization and a new dual-wielding playstyle. CDPR released a similar update to tie into the first season. The Cyberpunk 2077 Edgerunners update added a short questline that let players track down the cool yellow jacket the protagonist of Season 1 wore. There’s a good chance the new update will come with some similar surprises when it drops on October 22.

More details about the Edgerunners 2 update will be revealed today, October 21, 2026, during a special episode of REDstreams.

Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

items.title: Patch 2.31
items.summary: Patch 2.31 for Cyberpunk 2077 is now live! This update includes an AutoDrive upgrade and Photo Mode adjustments. It also addresses common issues encountered by players. For details, check the full list of changes below: Vehicles Updated Aut
items.content:
Patch 2.31 for Cyberpunk 2077 is now live!

This update includes an AutoDrive upgrade and Photo Mode adjustments. It also addresses common issues encountered by players. For details, check the full list of changes below:

Vehicles

  • Updated AutoDrive. When driving to a selected point, the vehicle now drives smoothly, overtakes blocking vehicles and no longer stops at traffic lights. Free Roam mode has also been upgraded to follow traffic rules and navigate the city more reliably.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Johnny always spawned in the passenger seat when using the Delamain Cab service.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where applying CrystalCoat to the Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru caused its wheels to flash in different colors.

    [/*]

Photo Mode

  • Most of the new poses introduced in Update 2.3 now work with any gender.

    [/*]

  • Disabled NPC collision, which will make it easier to position NPCs on top of other objects with collision (e.g. on car hoods).

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where some of the poses didn't work for Royce.

    [/*]

Quests & Open World

  • Freedom - Fixed the journal entry that appears when the player chooses not to steal the Rayfield Caliburn "Mordred."

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Fixed an issue where, after V fails to pursue and stop Semimaru and receives a text from River saying he'll contact V soon, the follow-up message never arrives.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Fixed an issue where the Yaiba Semimaru could flip over during the chase, preventing the player from entering it.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - It's no longer possible to trigger the quest if River died during The Hunt.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Players can now acquire the Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru through AUTOFIXER even if they failed The Hunt, which normally unlocks the side quest where the vehicle is obtained.

    [/*]

  • Nitro (Youth Energy) - Fixed a game crash that could occur in certain circumstances after leaving the Yaiba showroom event.

    [/*]

  • Nitro (Youth Energy) - Fixed an issue where the proxy interface UI in the Yaiba showroom is cut off when the "Larger HUD Elements" setting is enabled.

    [/*]

Miscellaneous

  • Fixed several localization and lipsync issues in various languages.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle to disable vignette. It can be found in Settings → Graphics → Basic.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on PC and Mac where Ray-Traced Reflections might not display correctly when enabled under certain conditions.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several issues with displaying text messages from Delamain.

    [/*]

  • Various fixes for fluff vendors.

    [/*]

PC-specific

  • Fixed an issue where NVIDIA Reflex could be disabled while DLSS Frame Generation was enabled, causing the screen to turn pink.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Path Tracing didn't activate properly in certain scenarios.

    [/*]

Mac-specific

  • Fixed an issue where changing graphics presets on Mac set Screen Space Reflections to a higher setting compared to the equivalent presets on PC.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue causing a permanent white screen when Frame Generation is enabled while entering the braindance in The Information.

    [/*]

  • Selecting "Defaults" in Video Settings no longer turns HDR Mode off.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where setting the MetalFX DRS Maximum Resolution above the value applied by the “For this Mac” preset could cause visual artifacts.

    [/*]

  • Fixed the inverted behavior of the "Mute Game in Background" toggle in Settings.

    [/*]

  • Removed the outdated "(Requires Game Restart)" disclaimer from the mouseover description of the "Disable Spatial Audio" setting.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on the App Store version that caused the game to become stuck on the “Press Space to continue” breaching screen.

    [/*]

  • Various stability and performance optimizations.

    [/*]
